title: No residuals for filmed TV shows and the union leadership
summary: Callender complains that musicians get residuals only on live-audience shows because Petrillo misjudged television.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: No. We only get residuals on the live ones, like Flip Wilson or Carol Burnett, but that's because they were done before a live audience. Other than live audience shows, the band gets nothing. That's one of the beefs we've had. Our leadership is really not on our side in some cases.
You're talking about the leadership of the Musicians Union.

Yeah, the union leadership. They haven't been realistic. Like, it was blown way back in the days of Petrillo, when TV first came out. Alvin Stoller has a newspaper clipping he took out that shows a Petrillo quote that he really didn't believe that TV was going to last. That's a fact! He thought it was a gimmick. So consequently, the musicians' contract with the TV networks regarding filmed shows was ridiculous. We get nothing. And I see shows, like the Life of Riley, for instance, that I get nothing for, and they still show it. Like, on Channel 58 you still see episodes of that. And hundreds of other
shows that we get nothing for. Only the ones that happen to be live.
That's so ridiculous. Because you're putting the same effort into the music.

The same music, the same effort, and the same notes. But that's just a terrible contract. I hope someday that somebody is able to do something about it, because the musicians get a royal screwing on that one.
Absolutely. I did not realize that.
We only get... Well, I said it before, so there's no point in repeating it. Only on shows with live audiences do the musicians get residuals.
